_comment: Public page routes deliberately NOT linked from the landing page, each with
the reason. A ratchet in both directions: a new entry means somebody shipped
a page nobody can reach, and an entry that stops being true must be deleted
in the same commit that links it — the known_failures.txt rule, for the same
/gas was the first thing this caught: a real public page — live gas across
seven chains, whose own meta description promises 'unreadable chains omitted,
never invented' — linked from nowhere. It is in the footer now rather than in
this file, which is the outcome this list exists to force.

routes./reset: Password-reset entry. Reached only by the emailed link, and it carries a token — advertising it on the landing page invites people to load it without one, which can only render an error.
routes./verify: Email-verification entry, same shape as /reset: the link IS the credential.
routes./wallet-link: Entered from the wallet-connect flow with state already established. Landing straight on it out of context has nothing to act on.
routes./signal: One signal's thesis, opened from a stream row as /signal?key=. A bare landing link has no id, so the page can only say the link has none.
routes./admin: The operator's settings page. It is linked from the dashboard for the operator only; every other account would land on a refusal, so the public landing page does not advertise it.
routes./study: The address people guess for the Study Room, whose door is labelled that; it answers a navigation page to /learn and is not a page of its own, so the landing page links /learn.
routes./marketplace: Old address for the agent catalogue. It answers a navigation page to /agents, which the landing page already links, so it is not a second page.
routes./market: Old address for the markets view. It answers a navigation page to /dashboard#markets. The landing page links the dashboard rather than this alias.
routes./botcheck: The custodial-bot check is served only when BOTCHECK_ENABLED is 1, true, yes, or on. Otherwise the page answers 404, so the landing page must not link a door that is closed.
routes./rwa: behind the RWA flag, off. It answers 404.
routes./rxb: Behind RXB_ENABLED. While the flag is off the public gets 404, so the landing page must not advertise it.
routes./fvb: behind FVB_ENABLED, off by default. The public gets 404. An operator gets an admin preview.
routes./hrc: Operator preview of the Hyperliquid borrow-rate cap. The public gets 404, including while HRC_ENABLED is on, so the landing page does not advertise it.
routes./cgc: Conservation-brake status behind CGC_ENABLED, off by default. Admin-only: a non-admin gets 404 even when the flag is on. It is not a public dashboard, so the landing page does not link it.
routes./srb: 404 for the public while SRB_ENABLED is off. There is no public dashboard, so the landing page does not advertise it.
routes./cover-adl: ADL re-entry cover is not offered. COVER_ADL_ENABLED is off for the public and the route answers 404; an admin can preview. A landing link would advertise a product waiting on an AFM licence review.
routes./cover-stopgap: Parametric stop-gap cover is not offered. COVER_STOPGAP_ENABLED is off for the public and the route answers 404; an admin can preview. A landing link would advertise a product waiting on an AFM licence review.
routes./tools: behind SAR_ORACLE_ENABLED flag, off. It answers 404. The catalog is the operator's, and the landing page does not link it.
routes./t2c: Admin-only duration signal. It answers 404 for everyone who is not the operator, including while the flag is on, so the landing page has no public door to it.
routes./qch: Quantum custody haircut behind QCH_ENABLED, off by default. Admin-only: a non-admin gets 404 even when the flag is on. It is not a public dashboard, so the landing page does not link it.
routes./xnav: Exit-adjusted NAV. Admin-only, and XNAV_ENABLED is off by default. A non-operator gets 404 even when the flag is on, so the landing page does not advertise it.
routes./claw-firewall: Behind DRAIN_FIREWALL_ENABLED, off unless it is 1 or true. While it is off the public gets 404, so the landing page does not advertise a closed door.
